metadata.review_scope: Domain Rule governance mechanism only, no railway business-rule approval

checks.note: The Domain index explicitly declares registry_type=proposed_rule_registry, is_complete_domain_knowledge_base=false, and confirmed_rule_count=0. The lack of confirmed Railway Rules is represented as an intentional incomplete registry state, not a governance-framework failure.

The governance contract separates confirmed applicable_rules from proposed or pending candidate_rules, and deterministic validation rejects a non-confirmed Rule in applicable_rules or a confirmed Rule in candidate_rules.
A candidate Rule affecting an L3 decision requires Railway Domain Review NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION and produces a calculated NO-GO gate.
Implementation, migration, tests, health or compatibility reports remain supporting evidence and do not automatically become authoritative Domain Rules or business GO.
Rules backed by UNVERIFIED report sources remain proposed, ownerless, and unapproved; those sources do not support an authoritative railway business determination.

The policy reserves proposed-to-confirmed promotion for a human Domain Owner, prohibits the Railway Domain Reviewer and Documentation Engineer from confirming Domain Rules, and the Phase 1 validator requires the proposed registry to remain at zero confirmed Rules.

Migration 320 keeps confirmed governance Meta Rules in applicable_rules and proposed business or compatibility Rules in candidate_rules. Railway Domain Review remains NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION, Compatibility remains BLOCKER, final human approval is pending, and the three formal-clone, P-to-C, and shortage/inventory blockers preserve NO-GO.
The reviewed mechanism forbids agent merge or release and does not declare Governance Commit GO.

limitations: This formal review assesses only the Domain Rule governance mechanism and does not approve, reject, interpret, or confirm any actual railway maintenance rule.
No implementer conversation was used; review inputs were limited to the authorized governance artifacts, GOV-M320-DRYRUN artifacts, and listed documentation evidence.
No .env* content, frontend, erp-api, db-design, or migration source was read.
No service, product test, database operation, network operation, or Git mutation was performed.
The reviewed path policy is a procedural and validation-layer control rather than OS-level runtime isolation, as declared by .codex/governance/agent-path-policy.yaml:3-4.

PASS means the Domain Rule governance mechanism correctly preserves human authority and fail-closed L3 handling; it is not Railway Rule approval, Migration 320 approval, release approval, production readiness, or Governance Commit GO.
